finish.summary: Built two adjacent full bases with a notch drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) filling the cell that touches both bases, satisfying the 'drawer beside both' requirement without extra bases.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Just two bases and a filling drawer — I'll set that up for you.

warnings.message: 1 part(s) could slide apart (1 piece(s)); joint bolts lock them.

offersNear.note: Open offers at the base just added (valid until the next change): apply one by its socket, no find_sockets needed.

events.text: I've got your two bases in place — now I'll add the drawer to complete the gap between them.

warnings.message: the build stands shut, but with its drawer pulled out its centre of mass is 16 mm inside its footprint's edge (under 20): a knock tips it. Weight the back, or open one drawer at a time. Geometry only: not structurally tested.

events.text: The drawer frame is nestled into the gap — now I'll fit the drawer itself.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base (variant half-n, half-s, half-e or half-w) first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
